item.title: Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-31T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>Welcome to the <a href="https://www.en.para.vetmed.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">Chair for Experimental Parasitology</a> at LMU Munich! Our department is at the forefront of research on protozoan parasites, <em>including Toxoplasma gondii, Plasmodium falciparum,</em> and <em>Trypanosoma brucei</em>. We explore the unique biology of these fascinating organisms, which possess distinct evolutionary histories and biological pathways that set them apart from other eukaryotes.</p> <p>Our research aims to uncover the similarities and differences between protozoan parasites and their hosts, which not only provides critical insights into fundamental biological processes but also holds the potential for developing novel therapeutic strategies.</p> <p>At our Chair, you'll be part of a dynamic and interdisciplinary team, collaborating on cutting-edge research in parasitology and benefiting from the resources and expertise of LMU Munich.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Qualifications: You hold a PhD in Biology, Biochemistry, or a related field. A strong interest in molecular parasitology and biochemical research approaches is advantageous.</li> <li>Work Experience: You have extensive experience in cell culturing and molecular and cell biology techniques. Experience with in vitro activity assays, immunoprecipitations, and Western blotting is highly desirable. Experience working with Toxoplasma gondii <em>Plasmodium falciparum</em> or other protozoan parasite genera is a plus</li> <li>Skills: You have solid knowledge of molecular biology techniques, such as PCR, cloning, protein expression and purification. Experience with quantitative proteomics and mass spectrometry is appreciated but not mandatory</li> <li>Soft Skills: You demonstrate excellent teamwork and communication skills, along with the ability to independently coordinate projects. A quick learner and the willingness to familiarize yourself with new technologies are essential. You are able to present your results clearly and concisely in English.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<p>We offer you the opportunity to join a dynamic and interdisciplinary research team lead by Prof. Meissner and Dr. Jimenez-Ruiz at the Chair for Experimental Parasitology at LMU Munich. The position is classified as a postdoctoral researcher within the state collective agreement (<a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">TV-L E13</a>), with an annual gross salary ranging from €57,000 to €65,000, depending on qualifications and experience. The position is initially limited to one year, with the possibility of extension contingent upon successful acquisition of additional funding.</p> <p>The position is full-time (40 hours per week), with flexible working hours and the option for home office arrangements.</p> <p>Additional Benefits:</p> <ul> <li>Work-life balance: 30 working days of vacation per year.</li> <li>Childcare support: Access to holiday and emergency childcare and family-friendly LMU services available via the Office for Equality and Inclusion.</li> </ul> <p>For more information on LMU Munich as an employer, please visit our <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/academic-careers/">career page</a> and our <a href="https://www.en.para.vetmed.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">department page</a>.</p>

Contact: <p>We look forward to receiving your application! If you are excited about the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research on protozoan parasites and are ready to take on an exciting challenge, please submit your application before <strong>01.09.2025</strong></p> <p>To apply, please send your CV, a cover letter outlining your research interests and qualifications, and contact details for at least two references to <a href="mailto:sekretariat@para.vetmed.uni-muenchen.de">sekretariat@para.vetmed.uni-muenchen.de</a>. We encourage you to contact us with any questions or for further information about the position.</p> <p>For more details, feel free to reach out to:</p> <p>Dr. Elena Jimenez-Ruiz<br /> <a href="https://www.en.para.vetmed.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">Chair for Experimental Parasitology</a><br /> Tel: +49 (0) 89 / 2180-3612<br /> e-mail: <a href="mailto:elena.jimenez@lmu.de">elena.jimenez@lmu.de</a></p> <p>We are happy to answer any inquiries and are available via email or phone to provide additional information.</p>

item.title: Doctoral Researcher (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Chemistry and Pharmacy

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-30T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The <a href="https://www.genzentrum.uni-muenchen.de/research-groups/bohlen/index.html">AG Bohlen</a> at the <a href="https://www.genzentrum.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">Gene Center</a> of LMU Munich is a research group in molecular biology focusing on regulated mRNA translation, tRNA biology, and immune regulation. We explore how translational control shapes cellular responses in development, disease, and immunity, using cutting‑edge molecular, biochemical, and cellular immunology techniques. Our lab fosters an intellectually rigorous, collaborative, and inclusive research culture.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>We are looking for a candidate who:</p> <ul> <li>Holds an excellent master’s degree (M.Sc./equivalent) in molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology, genetics, or a related field.</li> <li>Has hands‑on experience in molecular cloning, cell culture, RNA‑based assays, and ideally translation or tRNA methodologies.</li> <li>Ideally possesses immunology techniques (e.g., flow cytometry, ELISA, functional assays).</li> <li>Demonstrates strong analytical thinking, critical rigor, and motivation to push scientific frontiers.</li> <li>Is fluent in English (spoken and written); German is an advantage but not required.</li> <li>Has excellent communication skills and a teamwork mindset.</li> <li>Has ambitious career aspirations in academic research or biotech/pharma.</li> </ul> <p><br/></p>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>A stimulating, supportive, and multidisciplinary research environment in one of Europe’s top molecular biology centers.</li> <li>Structured PhD training through the LMU Graduate School and Gene Center seminars.</li> <li>Access to cutting‑edge core facilities (omics, microscopy, FACS, proteomics).</li> <li>Collaborative opportunities with internal and external partners (e.g. Max Planck Institute, DFG-funded networks).</li> <li>Competitive remuneration (65 % TV‑L E13) and social benefits, including parental leave and pension schemes.</li> <li>Access to LMU’s international network and German life-science funding landscape.</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please submit your application as a single PDF (max. 15 MB) including:</p> <ol> <li>Cover letter (1 page) detailing your motivation and relevant experience</li> <li>Curriculum vitae (including publications)</li> <li>Master’s thesis abstract or equivalent writing sample</li> <li>Contact details for two academic referees</li> <li>Academic transcripts (B.Sc./M.Sc.)</li> </ol> <p>Send your application via email with the subject line <strong>„PhD position AG Bohlen – [Your Name]”</strong><br /> to: <strong><a href="mailto:bohlen@genzentrum.lmu.de">bohlen@genzentrum.lmu.de</a></strong></p> <p>Informal enquiries are welcome and can be directed to <strong>Dr. Jonathan Bohlen</strong> (email: <strong><a href="mailto:bohlen@genzentrum.lmu.de">bohlen@genzentrum.lmu.de</a></strong>).</p>

item.title: Research assistant for the DFG Emmy Noether Research Group “MerFolk between Myth, Everyday Life, and Afterlife. Dance Research Perspectives on Transf...
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of History and the Arts

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-09-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The disciplines of dance studies and performance are newly based at the Institute for Theater Studies at LMU since 2024. Through transregional collaborations with institutions in Munich, Germany, and internationally, dance research as an active discipline represents a balance between setting new accents and pursuing continuities in movement research in Munich.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You have an excellent master's degree (M.A.) in film or media studies, with knowledge/studies/focus in one or more of the following: African Studies, Latin American Studies, (North) American Studies, Black Studies, Diaspora Studies, Gender studies, Queer Studies, Trans Studies, Cultural Studies, or related subjects. You are motivated to develop a dissertation project analyzing contemporary media based on non-European/European archival materials with a focus on body/movement.</p>

Benefits:

<p>The two positions are to be filled on January 1, 2026. Emmy Noether Groups are subject to an evaluation process halfway through the project period. The position is therefore limited to 2,5 years, with the option of extension. After a successful interview, you will become part of a forward-looking research team consisting of two doctoral projects and the project leader. You will work in a collegial environment at the Institute for Theater Studies at LMU Munich and have full access to the LMU Graduate Center with a wide range of qualification opportunities and support in the form of individual counseling and coaching. You will be supported in your doctoral studies, publishing the results of your research within the project, providing organizational support for project activities (e.g., project meetings, workshops, conferences), and actively contributing to the administrative aspects of the project. A keen interest in archival work and an openness to new methods in digital humanities are expressly desired. The project work focuses on acquiring or incorporating modes of new-learning and supports (new) skills in non-european/european language and movement, connected to the research design. The working languages are primarily English and German.</p> <p>LMU Munich offers a workplace where equal opportunities are respected, migration biographies are valued, and an intersectional attitude toward diversity is promoted.<br /> Additional benefits include:</p> <ul> <li>Mobile working</li> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>Support with childcare (e.g., holiday and emergency care services)</li> <li>Health promotion offers</li> <li>Opportunity to purchase a job ticket (discounted use of public transport)</li> </ul> <p>LMU Munich is an equal opportunity employer and committed to enhancing the diversity of its faculty.</p>

Contact: <p>Please submit a compelling application with the following documents:</p> <ul> <li>Short cover letter</li> <li>Short CV (max. two pages)</li> <li>Outline of your research interest in MerFolk (max. two pages)</li> <li>Writing sample (e.g., a chapter of your thesis, or an article, max. five pages)</li> <li>Contact details of two references</li> </ul> <p>Please send the following application documents with the subject line MerFolk in German or English by <strong>September 15th, 2025</strong>, in electronic form only as a PDF file: <em>Subject: MerFolk – PhD Position - M.A. dance studies, theater studies, or performance studies;</em> Addressed to:  <a href="mailto:m.diagne@lmu.de">m.diagne@lmu.de</a>:</p> <p>Prof. Dr. Mariama Diagne<br /> Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München<br /> Department Kunstwissenschaften<br /> Theaterwissenschaft<br /> Georgenstr. 11<br /> 80799 München</p> <p>Applicants who are shortlisted will be invited to an interview. The selection interviews are expected to take place in the second week of October 2025 (calendar week 41). If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Mariama Diagne (<a href="mailto:m.diagne@lmu.de">m.diagne@lmu.de</a>).</p>

item.title: PhD Student in Bacteriology/Molecular Microbiome Science (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Biology

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-01T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The <a href="https://unterwegerlab.com/">Unterweger lab</a> has a strong interest in the bacterial type VI secretion system and bacteria-bacteria interactions in microbial communities. We are joining the Faculty of Biology at the LMU in Fall 2025 and will be located at the Biocenter. This PhD project is funded by a Germany-wide network on illuminating gene functions of the human intestinal microbiota. The focus of the project will be on genes that encode bacterial toxins for microbe-microbe interactions. There will be ample of opportunities to connect with other groups locally and nationally.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You are fascinated by microbiology and have a strong desire to learn and grow professionally. You have a Master’s degree in the biosciences or are close to completing such a degree. You are experienced with techniques in at least one of the areas of molecular microbiology, microbiome research, computational biology, and protein biochemistry. You thrive in a team and your writing and communication skills in English are excellent.</p>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Salary according to <a href="https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/c/t/rechner/tv-l/allg?id=tv-l-2025&matrix=1">TVL</a> E-13 (65%)</li> <li>Your workplace is located at the Campus Martinsried and is easily accessible by public transport</li> <li>Scientific training at one of Europe’s leading universities</li> <li>Membership in the Graduate School Life Science Munich</li> <li>Access to a Germany-wide network in microbiome science</li> <li>In addition, you can benefit from the various <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/additional-services/corporate-benefits/">LMU corporate benefits</a>.</li> </ul> <p>The LMU is committed to increase the proportion of women in its workforce and encourages qualified women to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>Please submit your application (one pdf document including a cover letter, CV, motivation letter of maximally one page, contact of two references) <strong>by 01.08.2025</strong> to <a href="mailto:daniel.unterweger@bio.lmu.de">daniel.unterweger@bio.lmu.de</a> and include the name of the position into the subject line. The exact starting date can be negotiated.</p> <p>Please let us know briefly in your cover letter through which medium/website/etc. you became aware of our job advertisement.</p>

item.title: Junior Researcher on Coastal Resilience (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-24T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Chair in Human Geography at the Department of Geography offers a junior researcher position (doctoral student) to support the research activities as parts of the Horizon European project <a href="https://www.geo.lmu.de/geographie/de/aktuelles/newsuebersicht/news/coast-scapes-project-secures-eu-funding-a-new-opportunity-for-coastal-resilience-research.html">COAST-SCAPES</a> led by Dr. Liang Emlyn Yang. This is a four-year research project with a consortium of 31 international partners who jointly aim to develop innovative strategies for enhancing coastal resilience across Europe and beyond.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p><strong>Required qualifications and experiences:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Education background in geography or related discipline in spatial planning, hydrological modeling, geo-informatics sciences, machine learning, big-data or artificial intelligence, with interests in modeling human-environment systems.</li> <li>Proven skills in qualitative as well as quantitative social science research are preferred. Experience in project management, workshop moderation and organization are advantages.</li> <li>Technic skills and experience would be helpful in terms of developing agent-based models, social network analysis, spatial analysis and mapping tools, related AI utilization and computing expertise.</li> <li>Excellent English language skill (written and oral) is prerequisite.</li> <li>Willingness to travel for work (field investigations, project meetings, workshops etc.) in Europe countries, as well as in China, Vietnam, Thailand, and other Asian coastal areas is necessary.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Additional assets of interest:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Expertise in mathematics, statistics, modelling and/or computer programming (e.g. R, Netlogo, Matlab, Python)</li> <li>Curiosity and interests in the environmental history, anthropology and culture at global coast regions and particularly in Southeast Asia</li> <li>Experience in outreach and communication work at the science-policy-interface</li> <li>Language skills (written and oral) in German, Chinese, and/or that in Southeast Asia countries.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<p>The position is negotiable regarding part working time. We seek to increase the share of women in scientific positions and therefore explicitly encourages women to apply.</p>

Contact: <p>Applications shall be submitted by filling the <a href="https://survey.ifkw.lmu.de/Coastalresilience/">online form</a> and uploading one merged PDF document, which shall include a motivation letter, detailed CV, list of publications, a brief research proposal (two or three pages), any relevant certificates and other supportive documents, and contact details of at least two potential references (letter of recommendation is not required).</p> <p>Applications will be considered if submitted by <strong>Sunday, 24 August 2025</strong> at Central Europe Time. We encourage early submissions, which would help disperse our workload of evaluations. An online interview is expected in middle September 2025.</p> <p>Questions can be drawn to Dr. Liang Emlyn Yang by e-mail (<a href="mailto:emlyn.yang@lmu.de">emlyn.yang@lmu.de</a>). Relevant information is available on the introduction page of the <a href="https://www.geo.lmu.de/geographie/de/aktuelles/newsuebersicht/news/coast-scapes-project-secures-eu-funding-a-new-opportunity-for-coastal-resilience-research.html">COAST-SCAPES</a> project at LMU Munich.</p>

A doctoral thesis with us offers you the opportunity to deepen your knowledge in preparative and analytical techniques: Biochemistry of proteins and nucleic acids and NMR spectroscopy. We collaborate intensively and in an interdisciplinary way, for example with research groups from electron microscopy and computational chemistry.</p>

item.title: PhD Student / Research Assistant (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Chemistry and Pharmacy

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Cutsail research group at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) Munich is seeking a highly motivated PhD student / research assistant for full-time, on-site work in the field of bioinorganic spectroscopy, with a particular emphasis on electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy.</p> <p>This position is part of a newly established research group (2025) in the Department of Chemistry (Inorganic Chemistry). Our group investigates fundamental questions in bioinorganic chemistry using advanced spectroscopic techniques to understand the structure and reactivity of complex metal-containing systems.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Completed bachelor’s and master’s degrees (or equivalent) in Chemistry or a closely related field</li> <li>Strong oral and written communication skills in English (required)</li> <li>German language skills are desirable</li> <li>Interest in inorganic spectroscopy and metalloenzymes</li> <li>Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multinational team</li> <li>Experience with EPR spectroscopy or related techniques</li> <li>Background in inorganic, bioinorganic, or coordination chemistry</li> <li>Experience in inorganic synthesis and/or Schlenk-line preparations</li> <li>Experience with scientific programming (e.g., MATLAB, LabView) is advantageous</li> <li>Experience performing quantum chemistry computations (e.g., DFT) is advantageous</li> <li>Familiarity with scientific instrumentation and electronics</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>TV-L (E13, 67%) collective agreement (<a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">Current TV-L pay table</a>)</li> <li>A three-year PhD contract</li> <li>Access to world-class research infrastructure at LMU’s High Tech Campus (Großhadern, Munich)</li> <li>Opportunity to build novel experimental infrastructure in a growing research group</li> <li>Access to advanced instrumentation and interdisciplinary collaborations</li> <li>A supportive and dynamic scientific environment</li> <li>Participation in symposia and conferences</li> <li>Opportunities for teaching and professional development</li> <li>Theater and culture: special events, discounts and vouchers</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please send your application materials as a single PDF file to Prof. Dr. George Cutsail, <a href="mailto:george.cutsail@cup.lmu.de">george.cutsail@cup.lmu.de</a>, <em>using GC-010 in the subject line</em>. Your application should include:</p> <ul> <li>Cover letter</li> <li>Curriculum vitae</li> <li>Academic transcripts</li> <li>Contact information for two references</li> </ul>

Institution: Faculty of History and the Arts

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The disciplines of dance studies and performance are newly based at the Institute for Theater Studies at LMU since 2024. Through transregional collaborations with institutions in Munich, Germany, and internationally, dance research as an active discipline represents a balance between setting new accents and pursuing continuities in movement research in Munich.</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You have an excellent master's degree (M.A.) in dance studies, theater studies, or performance studies, with knowledge/studies/focus in one or more of the following: African Studies, Latin American Studies, (North) American Studies, Black Studies, Diaspora Studies, Gender studies, Queer Studies, Trans Studies, Cultural Studies, or related subjects. You are motivated to develop a dance historiographical dissertation project based on non-European/European archival materials with a focus on body/movement.</p>

Benefits:

<p>The two positions are to be filled on January 1, 2026. Emmy Noether Groups are subject to an evaluation process halfway through the project period. The position is therefore limited to 2,5 years, with the option of extension. After a successful interview, you will become part of a forward-looking research team consisting of two doctoral projects and the project leader. You will work in a collegial environment at the Institute for Theater Studies at LMU Munich and have full access to the LMU Graduate Center with a wide range of qualification opportunities and support in the form of individual counseling and coaching. You will be supported in your doctoral studies, publishing the results of your research within the project, providing organizational support for project activities (e.g., project meetings, workshops, conferences), and actively contributing to the administrative aspects of the project. A keen interest in archival work and an openness to new methods in digital humanities are expressly desired. The project work focuses on acquiring or incorporating modes of new-learning and supports (new) skills in non-european/european language and movement, connected to the research design. The working languages are primarily English and German.</p> <p>LMU Munich offers a workplace where equal opportunities are respected, migration biographies are valued, and an intersectional attitude toward diversity is promoted.<br /> Additional benefits include:</p> <ul> <li>Mobile working</li> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>Support with childcare (e.g., holiday and emergency care services)</li> <li>Health promotion offers</li> <li>Opportunity to purchase a job ticket (discounted use of public transport)</li> </ul> <p>LMU Munich is an equal opportunity employer and committed to enhancing the diversity of its faculty.</p>

Contact: <p>Please submit a compelling application with the following documents:</p> <ul> <li>Short cover letter</li> <li>Short CV (max. two pages)</li> <li>Outline of your research interest in MerFolk (max. two pages)</li> <li>Writing sample (e.g., a chapter of your thesis, or an article, max. five pages)</li> <li>Contact details of two references</li> </ul> <p>Please send the following application documents with the subject line MerFolk in German or English by <strong>September 15th, 2025</strong>, in electronic form only as a PDF file: <em>Subject: MerFolk – PhD Position - M.A. dance studies, theater studies, or performance studies;</em> Addressed to:  <a href="mailto:m.diagne@lmu.de">m.diagne@lmu.de</a>:</p> <p>Prof. Dr. Mariama Diagne<br /> Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München<br /> Department Kunstwissenschaften<br /> Theaterwissenschaft<br /> Georgenstr. 11<br /> 80799 München</p> <p>Applicants who are shortlisted will be invited to an interview. The selection interviews are expected to take place in the second week of October 2025 (calendar week 41). If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Mariama Diagne (<a href="mailto:m.diagne@lmu.de">m.diagne@lmu.de</a>).</p>

item.title: Research Assistant (PhD Candidate) in Artificial Intelligence (m/f/x)

<p>We are a team of international researchers led by Prof. Stefan Feuerriegel to push the frontier of AI for decision-making. Our team is highly diverse and comes from different countries and areas (e.g., machine learning, statistics, economics, engineering). We develop, implement, and evaluate new AI algorithms to improve data-driven decision-making. Our team publishes regularly in the top-tier AI/ML conferences (e.g., <em>NeurIPS, ICML, KDD</em>) but also in application-oriented outlets (e.g. <em>Nature Communications, Management Science</em>). Importantly, our institute has a double affiliation with the <em>Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics, and Statistics</em>, which allows us to pursue a broad vision aimed at impact across teaching and research.</p> <p>Please visit our website for <a href="https://www.som.lmu.de/ai"><ins>further information</ins></a> about us. item.title: PhD student in Geomicrobiology / Environmental Microbiology (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-08-31T11:19:44+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at LMU Munich invites applications for one PhD position in Geomicrobiology/ Environmental Microbiology to experimentally investigate the diversity and activity of marine microbial communities in the context of climate change.</p> <p>Together with warming and acidification, ocean deoxygenation is considered one of the three major impacts of climate change in global oceans according to IPCC, and a main research scientific topic for organizations such as UNESCO or IUCN. In the DFG Emmy-Noether <a href="https://www.gomez-saez-lab.com/">Research Group in Biogeochemistry and Climate Change</a>, we investigate the effects of warming and deoxygenation on dissolved organic matter (DOM) sequestration, due to interactions with microbial communities and the marine carbon and sulfur cycles. By combining field work experiments with state-of-art laboratory techniques from different disciplines, we aim to decipher new links between microbes and DOM, in the context of a changing ocean.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>M.Sc. in Microbiology, Environmental Sciences, Microbial Oceanography or a related subject.</li> <li>Very good English skills that allow to communicate in an international working environment, and to read and write scientific publications in English.</li> <li>A high degree of scientific curiosity and willingness to explore new methods and ideas.</li> <li>Willingness to participate in research stays and expeditions to coastal and marine regions onboard research vessels for several weeks.</li> <li>Team player attitude and communication skills to work in a multidisciplinary network of cooperation partners from several institutes in Europe.</li> </ul> <p>Additional recommended skills and knowledge:</p> <ul> <li>Prior experience in laboratory analyses using molecular biology techniques such as DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, qPCR, high throughput sequencing.</li> <li>Experience with bioinformatics (e.g. processing of 16SrRNA, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics)</li> <li>Practice on analyzing large datasets with multivariate statistics (e.g. R, Matlab or Phyton).</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<p>Our interdisciplinary team welcomes new members and we offer you a dynamic, international and academically stimulating environment. LMU Munich is an equal opportunity employer and committed to enhancing the diversity of its faculty. We encourage female candidates to apply.<br /> This project will be supervised by Dr. Gonzalo V. Gomez-Saez and is funded by DFG (<a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">65%, TV-L-E13</a>) for a maximum time period of three years with a probation period of six months. The PhD candidate must start on November 1st 2025.</p>

Contact: <p>Applicants are asked to submit by e-mail a complete set of application documents including a motivation letter (max two pages), CV, copies of B.Sc. and M.Sc. certificates, copy in pdf of the M.Sc. thesis and contact (name and e-mail) of two referees to <a href="mailto:g.gomez@lmu.de">g.gomez@lmu.de</a>.</p> <p><strong>Deadline to apply is 31. August 2025</strong>. The interview of selected candidates will happen during mid-September and final decision will also be made during September. Please do not expect e-mails confirmation until the selection process is over.</p>
